worked_solution:
The integral is defined over a type II region.

First, we evaluate the inner integral by integrating with respect to $x$, treating $y$ as a constant:

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{0}^{\sqrt[3]{\pi /2}}{\int }_{0}^{{y}^{2}}\operatorname{sin}⁡{y}^{3}\,dx\,dy & ={\int }_{0}^{\sqrt[3]{\pi /2}}\operatorname{sin}⁡{y}^{3}[{\int }_{0}^{{y}^{2}}dx]dy \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{\sqrt[3]{\pi /2}}\operatorname{sin}⁡{y}^{3}[x]_{0}^{{y}^{2}}\,dy \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{\sqrt[3]{\pi /2}}\operatorname{sin}⁡{y}^{3}({y}^{2}-0)\,dy \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{\sqrt[3]{\pi /2}}{y}^{2}\operatorname{sin}⁡{y}^{3}\,dy\end{aligned}
$$

Then, we integrate with respect to $y:$

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{0}^{\sqrt[3]{\pi /2}}{y}^{2}\operatorname{sin}⁡{y}^{3}\,dy & ={[-\frac{\operatorname{cos}⁡{y}^{3}}{3}]}_{0}^{\sqrt[3]{\pi /2}} \\  & =-\frac{1}{3}(\operatorname{cos}⁡(\frac{\pi }{2})-\operatorname{cos}⁡(0)) \\  & =-\frac{1}{3}(0-1) \\  & =\frac{1}{3}\end{aligned}
$$
